title: SMAD: A Semantics-Guided Multi-Agent Framework for Unsupervised Time-Series Anomaly Detection
abstract: arXiv:2611.28348v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Time-series anomaly detection (TSAD) lacks a one-size-fits-all detector for heterogeneous data and anomaly types. Existing automation is limited by implicit objectives, potentially unreliable historical knowledge, or high computational costs. More fundamentally, it selects how to detect anomalies without explicitly defining what to detect. We propose SMAD, an LLM-based multi-agent framework that translates anomaly intent into executable, testable detection pipelines. Rather than selecting detectors against an implicit target, SMAD establishes a natural-language semantic contract grounded in measurable time-series properties, specifying target event patterns, expected score responses, and validation questions. translated_title: SMAD：一种面向无监督时间序列异常检测的语义引导多智能体框架
translated_abstract: 时间序列异常检测（TSAD）缺乏一种能够应对异构数据和多种异常类型的通用检测器。现有的自动化方法受限于隐式目标、可能不可靠的历史知识或高昂的计算成本。更根本的是，这些方法在选择“如何检测”异常时，并未明确界定“要检测什么”。我们提出SMAD，一个基于大语言模型（LLM）的多智能体框架，它将异常检测意图转化为可执行、可测试的检测流水线。SMAD不再针对隐式目标来选择检测器，而是建立了一个基于可测量时间序列属性的自然语言语义契约，明确规定目标事件模式、预期的分数响应以及验证问题。该契约同时约束检测器的构建与评估：LLM智能体提出流水线方案，而与契约匹配的合成干预则从目标序列中提供无需标签的证据，用于评估语义覆盖度并指导迭代优化。
tldr: SMAD提出了一种基于LLM的多智能体框架，通过自然语言语义契约明确“检测什么”，将异常检测意图转化为可执行、可测试的检测流水线，并利用来自目标序列的无标签合成干预证据来构建与评估检测器，从而实现无监督时间序列异常检测。
en_tdlr: SMAD is an LLM-based multi-agent framework for unsupervised time-series anomaly detection that translates anomaly intent into executable, testable pipelines via a natural-language semantic contract, using label-free synthetic interventions from the target series to construct and evaluate detectors.
